01.actor: Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat; a would-be thief
01.event: Rabbi Elazar, absorbed in Torah study in the lower market of Tzippori, left his cloak in the upper market; once a man came to take it
01.turn: the man found a serpent on the cloak
01.outcome: the cloak was guarded and not taken
01.summary: Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat was so absorbed in Torah that he studied in Tzippori's lower market while his cloak lay in the upper market. One time a man came to take the cloak and found a serpent guarding it.
01.reason: A habitual frame followed by a one-time event: a man tries to take the cloak and is stopped by a serpent. Two actions and a change, so it is a story.

02.actor: Pishon the camel driver's wife; Beit Hillel and Beit Shammai
02.event: Pishon's wife refused him in his absence
02.turn: Beit Shammai explain the Sages measured him by a defective standard
02.summary: Beit Hillel cite Pishon's wife, who refused her husband in his absence; Beit Shammai answer that he had mistreated her property and was treated accordingly.
02.missing: Any narrated sequence beyond the single act cited as evidence.
02.reason: One thing Pishon's wife did, cited in a legal debate, with no change or causality narrated; Jeff ruled this passage not a story.

03.event: she seized a saddlebag full of coins for her sustenance
03.outcome: the Sages could not take it from her
03.summary: Rabbi Shabbtai's daughter-in-law seized a saddlebag full of coins for her sustenance, and the Sages lacked the authority to take it back.
03.missing: Any further action or change beyond the seizure and the legal outcome.
03.reason: One event followed by a ruling-like outcome, cited as a precedent; under R-C0's 2026-10-25 limit that is not a story.

04.missing: The Damcharya incident is only alluded to as a ruling; the passage is a scholarly dispute.
04.reason: Rav Huna and Rav Hanan argue over a precedent in which Rav ruled; ordinary scholarly back-and-forth plus a bare ruling, with no narrated event.

05.event: he carried a lamp in R. Yehoshua ben Levi's place but not in R. Yohanan's
05.outcome: he would tell his servant why
05.summary: Rabbi Abbahu used to move a lamp on Shabbat in R. Yehoshua ben Levi's locale but refrained in R. Yohanan's out of deference, explaining this to his servant.
05.missing: A one-time event; this is a habitual practice analysed by the Gemara.
05.reason: A custom cited as evidence that leads nowhere, with the Gemara's analysis around it; no event follows the habit.

06.event: the Rabbis urged Rav Sheshet to marry and have sons
06.turn: he put them off, saying his daughter's sons are his sons
06.outcome: the Gemara explains he had become impotent from Rav Huna's long discourses
06.summary: The Rabbis told Rav Sheshet to marry and father sons; he deflected them by saying his grandsons count as sons. The Gemara explains the real reason: he had become impotent from waiting through Rav Huna's lengthy lectures.
06.missing: Narrated action beyond the exchange; the impotence is a background explanation.
06.reason: Mainly speech, with mild pressure and evasion and a real event (his impotence) supplied only in the Gemara's explanation; between borderline and not, so borderline.

07.missing: Any event beyond teaching and a rebuke.
07.reason: Rav challenges how a mishna was taught and the Gemara explains the reasoning; standard rabbinic dialogue with no event.

08.actor: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba; Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
08.event: R. Hiyya found R. Yehoshua ben Levi hurrying his grandchild to the synagogue with a makeshift head covering
08.turn: R. Yehoshua ben Levi explained with the verse linking teaching grandchildren to Sinai
08.outcome: from then on R. Hiyya would not eat breakfast before teaching his child
08.summary: Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba met Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi rushing his grandchild to study, barely dressed, and asked why. He answered with the verse comparing teaching one's grandchildren to standing at Sinai. From then on Rabbi Hiyya would not eat before teaching his child.
08.reason: An encounter, an action observed, an explanation, and a lasting change in R. Hiyya's behaviour: at least two actions and a change.

09.actor: a depositor; Rav Dimi; Rabbi Abba
09.event: a man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without instructions
09.turn: the claim came before Rabbi Abba
09.outcome: he awarded it to the claimant on the grounds that Rav Dimi was not wealthy and the claimant gave a mark
09.summary: A man deposited silk with Rav Dimi, who died without leaving instructions. The case came before Rabbi Abba, who awarded the silk to the claimant because Rav Dimi was not wealthy and the claimant identified it.
09.missing: Any action or change after the ruling; the rest is legal reasoning.
09.reason: There are real events (deposit, death) before the court rules, more than coming before a rabbi alone, but the passage is otherwise a ruling and its reasoning; between borderline and not, so borderline.

10.actor: Reish Lakish; Rabbi Elazar; Rabbi Yohanan
10.event: Reish Lakish demanded proof of priesthood from teruma and R. Elazar objected; later R. Yohanan made the same objection
10.turn: Reish Lakish realised R. Elazar had been quoting R. Yohanan
10.outcome: he looked at R. Elazar harshly and rebuked him for not citing his source
10.summary: A man testified before Reish Lakish that someone was a priest; Reish Lakish demanded he had seen him receive teruma, and R. Elazar objected. Later, before R. Yohanan, the same thing happened and R. Yohanan gave R. Elazar's objection. Reish Lakish turned a harsh look on R. Elazar and rebuked him for not saying it in R. Yohanan's name.
10.reason: Mainly speech across two hearings, but with real conflict and an action (the harsh look) and a realisation; R-C7 shape 1, mainly speech but something happens.

11.event: a son-in-law passed by his father-in-law's house amid rumours about him and his mother-in-law
11.summary: A son-in-law suspected of intimacy with his mother-in-law walked past his father-in-law's door, and Rav Sheshet had him flogged.
11.missing: The incident is cited as evidence and only sketched.
11.reason: An incident only alluded to as a counter-example, though it has an act and a punishment that changes something; borderline rather than not.

12.missing: Any event besides a ruling imposed on an alleyway.
12.reason: A report of a ruling on a Nehardea alleyway followed by legal analysis; nothing happens to anyone.

13.event: Rav Malkiyyu married the deaf-mute to a woman and wrote her a 400-dinar marriage contract
13.summary: Rav Malkiyyu married off a deaf-mute neighbour and wrote his wife a marriage contract from the man's property; Rava praised him and the Gemara explains his reasoning.
13.missing: Any response or consequence within the narrative beyond praise and reasoning.
13.reason: A bare report of a rabbi's legal act, cited for its reasoning and praised, with nothing following; R-C5.

14.missing: A one-time event; this is a practice cited as proof.
14.reason: A custom of drawing water from a channel by the elders' authority, cited as legal evidence, leading nowhere.

15.missing: Any event beyond a question and answer.
15.reason: Rav Yirmeya asks Rav whether he has begun abstaining and Rav answers yes; a question and answer cited for a ruling.

16.missing: Any event besides a case brought to Rav Yehuda and his ruling.
16.reason: A case came before Rav Yehuda and he ruled; coming before him is the only event, inside a legal discussion.

17.actor: the widow of Rav Yosef son of Rav Menashya; Rav Yosef
17.event: she came before Rav Yosef and asked him to apportion sustenance and wine, which he did
17.turn: she then asked for silk garments and he asked why
17.outcome: she answered: for you, your friends and their friends
17.summary: A widow came before Rav Yosef and had him apportion her sustenance and then wine. When she asked for silk and he asked why, she retorted that she should not be shamed before him and his colleagues.
17.reason: A courtroom exchange in which the rabbi's apportioning is an act that changes something, like Jeff's Ketubot 65a:10, which he called borderline; otherwise mainly dialogue.

18.actor: Rabbi Tarfon; a yevama; his students
18.event: a yevama came to perform halitza before R. Tarfon
18.outcome: he told the students all to call out 'he who had his shoe removed' three times
18.summary: Rabbi Yehuda recalls sitting before Rabbi Tarfon when a yevama came for halitza, and Rabbi Tarfon instructed all present to proclaim the verse three times.
18.missing: Any action or change beyond the case arriving and an instruction.
18.reason: A case comes before a rabbi and he gives an instruction, cited as evidence of practice; coming before him is the only event.

19.event: Rav Kahana asked Rav Ashi to recall testimony he did not remember
19.turn: Rav Ashi eventually remembered and testified, but Rav Kahana hesitated
19.outcome: Rav Ashi assured him he had remembered by his own effort
19.summary: Rav Kahana prompted Rav Ashi about testimony he could not remember. Eventually Rav Ashi remembered and testified, and seeing Rav Kahana uneasy, told him he had not relied on his prompting but had remembered by his own effort.
19.reason: Several actions (prompting, remembering, testifying, hesitation) with tension and a resolution; more than speech alone.

20.actor: Rabbi Elai, Rabbi Ya'akov bar Zavdi; Rabbi Shimon bar Abba
20.event: two scholars studying stood up as Rabbi Shimon bar Abba passed
20.turn: he told them they need not have stood
20.summary: Rabbi Elai and Rabbi Ya'akov bar Zavdi were studying when Rabbi Shimon bar Abba passed, and they rose for him. He told them they were not obliged, being greater scholars and engaged in Torah.
20.reason: One real event (standing) followed by a teaching, with little change; between borderline and not, so borderline.
